cells.tense: The direction is settled, and now the person moves with the pen in hand and nothing left to rehearse.
cells.act: weigh what you know before it leaves you
cells.ask: Before the next thing you know leaves you on this push, take one breath and weigh it first — same sentence after, to the same person, just one breath ahead of it.
cells.core:
You're headed somewhere and you're not debating the route anymore. What you know arrives fast and you act on it without argument — quick calls, no second-guessing, no one nearby needing to be convinced. Whoever is working alongside you finds things make sense when you're there, and you didn't have to raise your voice for that. You chose a destination and you're trusting what you see along the way.

Give yourself a little more time in the gap between knowing a thing and saying it. Weigh what you know before it leaves you once before this week ends. Nothing gets held back and nothing gets slower — one breath, then the same sentence, to the same person. What reads as certainty from outside will start to feel picked-up from inside. That's the whole change, and it's enough.
cells.sheetLine: You call it fast and it holds — give one breath before the word.
cells.verb: moving on a destination with the authority of settled structure
cells.place: on the way toward a goal, where direction holds through resistance

cells.tense: The push is running ahead of itself now, bracing at a destination that hasn't been drawn yet.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Tally one stretch of the push — what went in, what came out — and read the figures before the story. Change one thing only if they point at it, and then put the tally away.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward the goal, and the push has started setting its own pace — one more mile, one more fix, calls made faster than the situation can land. The energy is real and the direction is right; the trouble is you're already living at a version of the end that hasn't happened, arguing for it the whole way there. Anyone moving beside you feels the lean.

Take one stretch of the push and tally what went in against what came out. Read the figures first, talk second. If they point somewhere, change one thing. If they don't, you've spent an hour getting your own read back, and the whole drive settles for it. Counting this way isn't more grip — it's the way out of the lean.

cells.tense: The direction was chosen on some earlier day, and the one who chose it is still standing at that door.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Take what a finished chapter left behind and build the smallest next thing from it by hand, on your own, no announcement — let it take whatever time it takes.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the push, it stopped being yours. The direction holds and the effort still goes out, but it goes out on a decision made on an earlier day and not re-picked since. Resistance is still being met; what's missing is wanting the end. The one standing at the door is still attached to having chosen it. That isn't laziness — it's a motion burning old fuel.

Build the first new thing from what the clearing showed. Take what a finished chapter left in your hands and make the smallest version of the next thing from it — one piece, by hand, no announcement. Not a plan, not a whole structure, just the first piece. Movement comes back the way it went: through the hands, a little at a time, until the direction is chosen again.

cells.tense: The steering is happening all day and the hand on it isn't being claimed by anyone at all.
cells.ask: Take something that recently settled and hold it exactly where the change left it — not growing it, just steady, for as long as you can stand to leave it alone.
cells.core:
You're carrying this drive, and by your own accounting you're along for the ride. The pace, the calls, the sense the room picks up — it all reads as circumstance: a good quarter, a team that happens to run well, conditions lining up. Whatever you do between the decision and the destination gets filed under luck. The direction keeps holding and nobody's naming who holds it.

This gets simpler, not bigger. Take one thing that recently settled — a finished project, an arrangement, a changed way of doing something — and hold it exactly where the change left it. Not growing it. Just steady. Holding what an ending produced is its own work, and doing it with your own hands makes plain what the record already shows: the steering is yours, and it has been yours.

attempts.check: The draft wants to say what the destination is or how long the person has been pushing, and the record names neither — Command is structure moving, Drive is motion toward a destination, and nothing lists what's at the end or when it started. A reader could reasonably say pausing to weigh things mid-push is a stalled push, or that counting hours is just more control — and the asks survive that: each opens on its own verb (weigh, count, build, hold), is small, and returns something whether the read is right or wrong. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'decisions move with clarity and speed' — it flatters the card, so it stays off the glass and out of the core.
